correctness.rationale: From the source equation at omega=pi/2, x=lambda_0+1/2 in (0,1/2) satisfies cos(pi x)=t sin(pi x/2). Setting y=sin(pi x/2) gives 2y^2+ty-1=0 and the stated positive root. Source Theorem 3.5 gives D(D_0^L)=D(D^L)+span{u_0^L}, with u_0^L=phi r^{lambda_0^L}f_0^L. The minimal domain is H^1. The singular gradient is of order r^{lambda_0^L-1}, hence the polar p-integral converges exactly for p<2/(1-lambda_0^L) and is logarithmically divergent at equality. Monotonicity and endpoint limits follow by elementary differentiation.
